Welcome! I’m glad you’re here. Together, we’re about to step into a world that’s usually hidden from view—a place where daily life is shaped by secrets, resilience, and quiet ambition. Imagine, just for a moment, what it’s like to navigate the bustling rhythms of commerce and adaptation behind North Korea’s tightly guarded borders. It’s a side of the country most of us never get to see.
In Felix Abt’s unforgettable book, A Capitalist in North Korea: My Seven Years in the Hermit Kingdom, we’re invited to witness how entrepreneurship finds a foothold even within the grip of authoritarian rule. You’ll find yourself walking alongside Felix as he negotiates with officials, trains local staff, and learns to balance hope with caution—all while building businesses in a place where every move is watched, and every decision is influenced by politics and survival.
What really stands out is the way this story captures the ingenuity and determination of people striving for something better, even when the odds seem impossible. Through moments of connection, the occasional misunderstanding, and some truly unexpected friendships, you’ll see the human side of North Korea—a world shaped by the dreams and quiet strength of ordinary individuals. So, as we set out on this journey together, get ready to challenge your assumptions, discover the surprising ways hope can flourish, and glimpse life as it unfolds behind the headlines. Let’s explore what it really means to dream, adapt, and connect—even in the most unlikely of places.
